source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check logo design.
check info is correct.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Logo should be clear and no spelling error
2. Logo design should match with customer's requirement

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- "Menu Bar (row)" (row menu bar): verify the BMC web top/side menu navigation items render and are clickable. Agent loads the page and enumerates the menu items.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the list of menu items rendered in the row menu bar so user confirms navigation is correct.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL follows Items and invents a row-menu enumeration/clickability method, but the preserved Procedure tests logo design and unspecified information while Criteria accept only logo clarity, spelling and customer branding. A rendered menu-item list therefore cannot prove the written Procedure/Criteria, and the source supplies no menu inventory, routes or click result.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED tries to combine row-menu navigation, logo, identity information and role visibility into one matrix. Those safeguards are useful only after scope resolution; combining the conflicting branches does not establish which purpose is authoritative and would allow evidence from one branch to be reported for another.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 848/2291 repeats `Menu Bar (row)` as purpose and the logo criteria as expected output without identifying that they validate different UI objects or resolving the missing menu behavior criteria.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1011 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-34 permits BLOCKED when the core purpose and acceptance semantics conflict; ED-33 preserves the Master wording; ED-38 forbids claiming DUT coverage or retrying automatically and keeps the verdict engineer-owned.

original_test_intent: Unresolved. Items identifies a horizontal/row menu-bar test, while the Procedure directs a logo-design and generic-information check and Criteria judge only logo appearance and customer branding. The Master does not say whether logo/info are merely content within the row bar or whether menu rendering, item order, navigation and click behavior are intended checkpoints.
original_method: Unresolved. One source branch calls for observing logo design and information correctness; the other, introduced by Items and DeepSeek, calls for enumerating and clicking row-menu entries. Neither branch defines an authoritative menu inventory, expected routes, row orientation, information fields or a complete shared acceptance matrix.
manual_activity: An engineer must decide whether this source row is a row-oriented menu/navigation test, a logo/branding-information test, or an explicitly split set of checkpoints. After that decision, an operator may provide the approved UI reference and judge customer-specific visual appearance while browser automation exercises only the selected read-only scope.
required_inputs: Signed scope decision selecting menu/navigation, logo/branding and information checkpoints without changing the preserved Master row
If menu scope is intended: exact row/horizontal menu location, approved item labels/order, role/locale/viewport matrix, expected routes, enabled/disabled behavior and safe navigation-only exclusions
If logo scope is intended: approved customer logo asset/version, placement, dimensions, clarity/spelling/branding rules and responsible visual approver
If `info is correct` remains: named fields, authoritative read-only source, units/format/freshness and comparison tolerances
Immutable BMC identity, firmware/WebUI build, endpoint/certificate, protected role account, evidence-redaction rules and unexpected-action recovery
safety_requirements: Do not infer that menu items, logo and generic information are one test merely because they may share a header area; they have distinct controls and acceptance evidence.

Do not execute DeepSeek's clickability sweep before an engineer supplies the safe menu inventory. A menu can expose power, reset, firmware update, configuration or logout actions that are not navigation-only.
Do not use successful navigation as proof that customer branding is correct, and do not use a clear logo as proof that menu items render, are ordered correctly or reach the expected routes.
Do not clear dmesg, syslog, SEL or BMC audit logs. Preserve the existing baseline and collect only relevant read-only navigation evidence after scope approval.

Use an isolated authenticated browser, bind endpoint/certificate/BMC identity, redact credentials/cookies/serials and issue at most the approved navigation action once; no automatic retry on ambiguous route or response.
Stop if the authoritative scope, menu reference, branding reference, information source or safe-click exclusion cannot be defined.
agent_execution_scope: Before the engineer decision, preserve the source and collect only non-mutating documentation/UI-layout evidence; do not click an undefined menu set and do not claim either source branch complete.

After scope approval, automate only the explicitly selected read-only checkpoints with a fixed browser/role/locale/viewport and capture DOM, screenshot, route, response and authoritative-data correlation as applicable.
Keep menu rendering, navigation, logo/branding and information correctness as separately reported checkpoints even if the Project elects to retain them in one testcase.
Report uncovered original branches and Project Override coverage explicitly; never issue DUT PASS/FAIL or retry automatically.
engineer_actions: Resolve whether the authoritative purpose is row-menu navigation, logo/customer branding, generic information correctness or separately named checkpoints, and document why.
Approve the corresponding menu/route matrix and destructive-action exclusions or the logo/info reference and visual acceptance owner.
Review each selected checkpoint's evidence independently and issue the formal verdict without allowing one branch to stand in for another.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It follows the `Menu Bar (row)` label but does not follow the written `Check logo design` Procedure or logo-only Criteria. It also invents clickability without a safe item list or expected destination, so it is not an executable final method.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No browser command should be recommended until an engineer resolves the row-menu versus logo/info scope. Then use a bounded UI procedure for the selected checkpoints and explicitly exclude state-changing menu actions.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The row-menu Items label, logo/info Procedure, logo-only Criteria, absent Script and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved as conflicting source facts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create separate Review-layer checkpoints for row-menu layout, item enumeration, safe route navigation, logo/branding and named information fields only after an engineer states which are in scope; bind each checkpoint to its own authoritative expected result.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The BMC WebUI build, role, locale and viewport approved by the Project after scope resolution.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware and WebUI asset/build identifiers before any later execution.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/customer WebUI navigation specification, approved branding asset/style guide and vendor field/source documentation selected by the engineer.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Does not silently merge the Items/DeepSeek navigation interpretation with the Procedure/Criteria logo branch; it preserves the conflict and requires an explicit scope decision.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Menu presence or route success does not validate logo clarity/customer match; logo evidence does not validate menu inventory, order or click behavior; generic information requires its own named source comparison.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer scope decision, per-checkpoint expected matrix, safe-action exclusions, UI identity and evidence policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Blind menu activation can mutate BMC state; subjective customer branding needs an approved reference/owner; combined evidence can create a false coverage claim.

project_override_considerations: A Project may retain all UI checks in one testcase or select only a defined branch, but must record the preserved conflicting source, actual checkpoints, reason, engineer approval, per-checkpoint expected results, safe menu exclusions and any original branch left unverified. Missing references are readiness inputs only after the core scope conflict is resolved.
expected_evidence: Signed engineer decision aligning Items, Procedure and Criteria at the Review layer while retaining the original Master text
BMC firmware/WebUI build, endpoint/certificate identity, account role, locale, viewport and protected-session evidence
If menu is selected: approved row-menu inventory/order plus redacted DOM/screenshot and one-to-one route/navigation results for each safe item
If logo is selected: approved customer logo reference plus redacted rendered evidence and human visual annotations for clarity, spelling, placement and match
If information is selected: named displayed values with authoritative source, timestamp/freshness, units/format and comparison result
Explicit coverage ledger for every retained or omitted branch, proof no state-changing action occurred and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items says `Menu Bar (row)`, but Procedure says `Check logo design` and `check info is correct`, while Criteria judge only logo clarity, spelling and customer match. No source text connects those logo/info checks to menu enumeration or defines menu behavior. The identity, operation and acceptance branches therefore do not form one determinate testcase.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is not blocked merely by a missing browser package or Project reference. The authoritative purpose and acceptance criteria conflict: selecting navigation, branding or a merged interpretation would change coverage. An engineer must resolve the core scope before a safe execution handoff can be produced.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its unsupported menu enumeration/clickability method as a complete interpretation; retains it only as a candidate branch selected from Items.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Changes PACKAGE to BLOCKED because its combined menu/logo/info matrix masks the unresolved source scope rather than resolving it; its identity, role, route and redaction safeguards remain useful after a decision.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces the unexamined coexistence of menu purpose and logo criteria with explicit source-conflict ownership and no-execution boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a menu-item list or successful clicks from being reported as customer-logo validation, and prevents subjective logo evidence from being reported as proof of row-menu navigation coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A WebUI header can contain a logo, informational widgets and horizontal navigation, but these are separate UI objects. Rendering verifies presence/layout, navigation verifies route and authorization behavior, branding verifies an approved visual asset, and information correctness requires a named authoritative data source. Because this row's Items, Procedure and Criteria name different objects and never define their relationship, automation cannot recover the intended coverage without inventing it.
